column3: Directly supports the messenger-to-all-people clause and frames the mission through warning and glad news.
Distinguishes unintentional error from what hearts deliberately intend, clarifying personal responsibility.
Links wrongdoing, a bad occurrence, and replacement with good, supporting the focus contrast between harm and good.
Makes guidance and going astray return upon the individual self while denying that the messenger is their keeper.
The nearby passage frames obligation, fear, and the absence of injustice; it supplies the surrounding liability context.
Shows a messenger sent to a people as an explicit warner, supporting the focus's public messenger role.
Places sending a messenger among modes of divine communication, supporting source and messenger distinction.
The immediately preceding verse contrasts people's attribution of good and bad occurrences and attributes all to God.
Names the prophet as sent witness, bearer of glad news, and warner, closely matching the focus's messenger and witness clauses.
Combines sending the messenger with God as sufficient witness, a close structural parallel to the focus.
Limits the messenger's burden to his own self, supporting bounded personal liability though in a different setting.
A messenger is sent as a witness over a people, directly reinforcing messengerhood and testimony.
Answers denial of messengerhood with God as sufficient witness, closely matching the final focus clause.
Its ordering of relational claims through the self is only a remote connection to individual liability.
Sets doing good against bad and presents good as the means of repelling bad.
Pairs a bad act with proportionate recompense and allows pardon and reform, relevant to accountable consequences.
Defines obedience to the messenger and denies that he was sent as a guardian over those who turn away.
Affirms that the addressee belongs to the sent messengers but adds little about attribution or responsibility.
Attributes favor to God and calls God sufficient in knowledge, a limited parallel to divine source and sufficiency.
Carefully separates accidental killing from intentional action and assigns a remedial consequence to the accidental case.
Explicitly identifies the speakers as a messenger of the Lord, supporting the commissioned-messenger theme.
God testifies to what was sent down and is sufficient as witness, closely supporting the focus's testimony clause.
Connects a group's reversal to what it earned, supplying an accountability pattern but not the focus's good/bad formulation.
Presents signs in horizons and selves until truth is clear, then invokes the Lord as sufficient witness.
Contrasts a good occurrence and a bad occurrence in opponents' reactions, but does not address their source or self-liability.
The self and pairing material is not materially connected to the focus beyond a shared self term.
The formed self provides a conceptual background for the focus's statement about what comes from one's self.
Names an occurrence that befalls the addressee and joins it to steadfast conduct, supporting the event-and-response dimension.
Contrasts spoken obedience with contrary hidden planning; God records it and is sufficient as trustee.
Explicitly makes doing good and doing bad return to one's own selves, strongly supporting personal causal share.
Assigns each advocate a share in a good or bad intervention, directly supporting personal participation in outcomes.
Makes deliberate killing carry an explicit grave consequence, a strong liability contrast with the accidental case.
Combines warning with glad news and a good recompense, supporting the messenger's announced consequences.
Contrasts reactions to a good occurrence and an affliction but concerns opponents' response rather than attribution.
This conflict instruction has little bearing on the focus's attribution, messenger, or witness claims.
Commands reliance on God and calls God sufficient as trustee, a limited parallel to the closing sufficiency formula.
Makes sight and blindness return upon each self and denies that the speaker is a keeper over the audience.
Makes persons witness against their own selves, a relevant but broader form of individual accountability.
Sending the she-camel as a trial shares only the sending form, not the focus's messenger or responsibility relation.
States that a bad occurrence reaches people because of what their hands put forward, strongly supporting causal self-liability.
The claim of no discrepancy in the Quran is not materially connected to the focus.
Its general recompense for doers of good offers only a broad good-outcome connection.
God's ownership and sufficiency as trustee echo divine sufficiency, but not the focus's witness or attribution relation.
Different ranks for those acting and sitting provide only a general action-and-result connection.
The question of sufficient angelic support is not a substantive parallel to the focus.
The phrase good example is not enough to connect this covenantal scene to the focus.
Deliberate harm requires measured compensation, a specific accountability analogy supported by the package channel.
Directly contrasts good and bad deeds with differentiated recompense, supporting accountable outcomes.
The inward remembrance instruction has no substantive link beyond the word self.
Requires reports to be returned to the messenger and qualified authorities, supporting a bounded messenger role in public matters.
Restricts recompense to what people did, supporting accountability but without the focus's source distinction.
A messenger is sent from among a people with a public summons, supporting the focus's sent-to-people clause.
Names people as wronging their own selves and treats their situation as accountable, though it lacks the good/bad contrast.
God is witness over everything, supporting the broad witness premise without messengerhood.
Distinguishes a messenger's witness while present from God's continuing witness, closely supporting bounded messenger responsibility.
Says gratitude benefits one's own self while God is self-sufficient, supporting personal return of response.
States that schemers scheme only against their own selves, a relevant self-return pattern despite its indirectness.
Explicitly calls Jesus God's messenger and ends with God sufficient as trustee, but not as witness.
A striking occurrence reaching whom God wills is only a distant event-occurrence parallel.
The beautiful reward scene has no clear link to the focus's attribution or messenger role.
The prophet's grief over disbelief is not a substantive parallel to the focus.
Requires a greeting to be returned equally or better and makes God reckoner, a limited accountability pattern.
The recurring opposition to prophets and divine guidance supports messenger context only indirectly.
Mocks the one sent as messenger, supporting the social reception of messengerhood but not liability or testimony.
The isolated question naming the Crusher has no usable relation to the focus.
Messengers bring clear proofs before consequences, supporting the idea that a public mission precedes accountability.
Guidance for people and witnessing a month are not a sufficiently specific parallel to the focus.
The gathering and truthfulness statement does not materially address the focus's three claims.
Confirms that messengers delivered their Lord's messages under encompassing knowledge, supporting accountable transmission.
Shows a bad act being seen as good and removes the prophet from responsibility for their response.
The fire reaching hearts is too fragmentary and unrelated to the focus.
The divided response to belief and the warning of a blaze are only remote background.
A messenger recites clear signs to bring believers from darkness into light, supporting the messenger's declared public function.
Makes conduct such as withdrawal, non-fighting, and offering peace determine whether a claim lies against people.
Challenges those who do bad deeds and calls their judgment bad, a general evil-and-consequence connection.
Contrasts claimed speech, inner knowledge, and divine knowledge, supporting the limits of a messenger's accountable speech.
An affliction reaches people because of what they made, supporting consequence linked to their own action.
Multiple messengers are sent and rejected, supporting messengerhood but not the focus's other claims.
Calls the messenger a witness over the community and the community witnesses over people.
Conditions a response on observable conduct, supporting liability tied to action in a nearby legal setting.
Bad deeds are made attractive and lead to misguidance, a related but indirect bad-as-good inversion.
Records objection to God sending a human messenger, supporting the disputed messenger-sending theme.
The isolated description of extended columns has no usable relation to the focus.
Directly says the addressee was sent and defines that sending in relation to all worlds.
Concealing clear guidance from people is not a close parallel to the focus.
Requires verification before judging someone who offers peace, supporting responsibility for one's assessment and action.
People reject messengers with clear proofs, while God is self-sufficient, supporting messenger reception and divine independence.
The feared arrival of divine might is not a close relation to the focus.
Returning and bringing forth from the earth is unrelated to the focus.
Sending devils against deniers is not a usable parallel to sending a messenger to people.
The pilgrimage remembrance instruction is unrelated to the focus.
Moses's inward fear is not a substantive parallel to self-caused bad outcomes.
The instruction to remember God on counted days is unrelated to the focus.
Directly contrasts multiplied return for a good deed with equal return for a bad deed and denies injustice.
Opposition to God and His messenger carries punishment, but it adds little to the focus's specific relation.
Sending a violent storm is not a usable parallel to messenger sending or self-liability.
Turning away from signs gives only remote context for how people receive a message.
Denial despite inward certainty is called wrongdoing and arrogance, supporting culpability located within selves.
The closing phrase naming two classes of whisperers has no usable relation to the focus.
Bodily testimony about what people did strongly supports accountable witness and personal action.
The addressee is sent with truth as a bearer of glad news and warning, while not held to account for the people of the Fire.
Guidance of people is explicitly not placed upon the addressee, preserving divine guidance alongside the messenger's bounded role.
Every self is fully repaid for what it earned and is not wronged, directly supporting accountable consequences.
Each self receives what it earned and bears what it acquired, a direct formulation of personal moral return.
The messenger's duty is stated as notification after people accept or turn away, closely supporting limited messenger responsibility.
Denies that the addressee has a share in the decisive matter, supporting the distinction between messenger agency and divine decision.
Every self is fully repaid for what it earned, with no injustice, directly supporting individual consequence.
God's favor includes sending a messenger from among the believers to recite, purify, and teach them.
Consequences are tied to what hands sent forward, while God is not unjust to servants.
Messengers are sent to be obeyed by God's permission, directly linking commissioned messengerhood and divine source.
The Book is sent down to the messenger so that he may judge among people by what God has shown him.
Whoever does wrong or wrongs the self and then seeks forgiveness finds God forgiving and merciful.
Whoever earns a sin earns it only against the self, a direct parallel to the focus's self-liability clause.
Earning a fault or sin and casting it upon an innocent person makes the doer bear the resulting burden.
Whoever does evil is recompensed for it and finds no protector or helper apart from God.
Messengers bring glad news and warning so people have no argument before God after their coming.
The messenger has come with truth from the Lord, directly reinforcing his public commission.
A proof has come to people from their Lord and a clear light has been sent down, supporting public divine communication.
Messengers come to explain after an interval, preventing people from claiming no bearer of glad news or warning came.
The messenger is commanded to convey what was sent down from his Lord; God protects him from people.
After the commands, the messenger is charged only with clear delivery.
Nothing lies on the messenger except delivery, a close direct parallel to the focus's bounded messenger role.
Addresses believers through their own selves and says another's going astray does not harm them when they are guided.
Harm and good touched by God are placed under divine power, supplying a source-side parallel to the focus's attribution of good.
Those who do evil in ignorance and then repent and reform meet God's forgiveness and mercy.
Every self is held in pledge for what it earned, directly supporting personal consequence.
The addressee is neither made guardian over people nor trustee for them, closely supporting limited messenger responsibility.
Messengers from among their communities recount divine signs and warn of the meeting, supporting public messengerhood and accountability.
No bearer carries another's burden; each person's return is to God for what they differed about.
The speakers acknowledge that they have wronged their own selves and seek divine forgiveness and mercy.
Messengers come to the children of Adam reciting signs; those who respond rightly have no fear or grief.
The messenger is sent to all people and calls them to faith in God and His messenger.
The messenger disclaims possession of benefit or harm for himself except what God wills, clarifying human and divine agency.
Human action is named while decisive efficacy is assigned to God, a useful causation parallel despite its battle setting.
An affliction is warned not to fall only on wrongdoers, qualifying simplistic individual attribution of collective events.
Consequences are tied to what hands sent forward, and God is not unjust to servants.
God does not change a favor bestowed on a people until they change what is within themselves.
God did not wrong past peoples; they wronged their own selves.
Some acknowledge their sins after mixing good work with another that is bad, directly joining good, bad, and personal responsibility.
People are told to act; God, His messenger, and the believers will see their work before return to the Knower.
A messenger has come from among the people, concerned by their hardship and eager for their good.
God does not wrong people at all; people wrong their own selves.
Whoever is guided is guided for the self, whoever goes astray does so against it, and the addressee is not a guardian over them.
Good deeds remove bad deeds, providing a direct good-and-bad accountability relation.
God does not change a people's condition until they change what is within themselves.
Those who repel bad with good receive a good final outcome, closely supporting the focus's good/bad contrast.
Every messenger is sent in the language of his people so he may make matters clear to them.
The deceiver denies coercive power and makes those who responded bear responsibility for themselves.
A messenger is sent to every community with the call to worship God and avoid false deities.
A witness is raised from every community, and the messenger is brought as witness over his community.
Divine willing and human action are held together, with people questioned about what they used to do.
Every self comes disputing for itself and is fully repaid for what it did without injustice.
Guidance benefits the self and misguidance is against it; no bearer carries another's burden, and punishment follows sending a messenger.
The truth is from the Lord while people are confronted with belief or refusal and their consequences.
Every self is recompensed for what it strives toward, directly supporting personal consequence.
Those who follow divine guidance neither go astray nor suffer, joining guidance and outcome.
The addressee states that he warns only by revelation, directly delimiting the messenger's function.
The scales of justice leave no self wronged, even by the weight of a seed.
A consequence is tied to what hands sent forward, while God is not unjust to servants.
The addressee identifies himself as a clear warner, directly supporting the messenger's announced role.
Messengers are sent in succession; repeated rejection follows, supporting the recurring public mission theme.
No self is burdened beyond its capacity, and a record speaks truth without injustice.
The messenger bears only what he is charged with, while the audience bears what it is charged with; his duty is clear delivery.
The addressee is sent only as a bearer of glad news and a warner.
Guidance is for one's own self, while the addressee is only one of the warners toward those who go astray.
A messenger is sent so people cannot cite what their hands sent forward as a reason no messenger came.
The Lord does not destroy communities until He sends a messenger in their center reciting signs.
Earlier peoples were not wronged by God; they wronged their own selves.
Corruption on land and sea appears because of what people's hands earned, so they may return.
Disbelief is against the disbeliever, while righteous action is prepared for one's own selves.
Each side is not questioned about the other's crimes or deeds, supporting differentiated responsibility.
No burdened self bears another's burden, and the addressee is a warner to those who fear their Lord.
No community has passed without a warner in it.
Nothing lies on the messengers except clear delivery.
The revelation warns whoever is alive and establishes the word against those who deny.
Gratitude is accepted for people, while disbelief does not benefit God; it supports response returning to the respondent.
Those who have exceeded against their own selves are called not to despair of God's mercy.
Every self is fully repaid for what it did, while God knows best what they do.
Every self is recompensed for what it earned; there is no injustice that day.
Good work is for the self and bad work is against it; the Lord is not unjust to servants.
Whatever affliction befalls people is because of what their hands earned, while much is pardoned.
The messenger's role is only delivery; human response to mercy and misfortune is then described.
The messenger receives revelation by divine command and guides to a straight path.
Whoever does good does so for the self and whoever does evil does so against it, then all return to their Lord.
Every self is repaid for what it earned, with no injustice.
The messenger disclaims independent knowledge of what will be done with him or the audience and follows revelation.
The messenger is sent as witness, bearer of glad news, and warner, a very close parallel to the focus.
The messenger is among the community; their following every preference would cause hardship, while faith is made beloved to them.
No bearer bears the burden of another, directly supporting individual liability.
A human being has only what he strives for, directly supporting personal causal share.
Each person's striving will be seen, linking action to witnessed assessment.
The person is then repaid with the fullest recompense.
Messengers are sent with clear proofs and the Book and balance so people may uphold justice.
Jesus announces a messenger coming after him, supporting continuity of commissioned messengerhood.
God sends His messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, supporting the divine source of the mission.
A messenger is raised among the unlettered people to recite signs, purify, and teach them.
No calamity occurs except by God's permission, while belief in God guides the heart.
The messenger disclaims power to cause harm or provide right guidance independently.
The messenger's charge is communication from God and His messages.
Every self is held in pledge for what it earned.
The human being is a witness against his own self.
The one who purifies the self succeeds.
The one who corrupts the self fails.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good sees it.
Whoever does an atom's weight of bad sees it.
